title: People Ops: Manager Guide — Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Feedback (2026)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This guide provides managers at Redwood Inference with a single-reference playbook for hiring, employee onboarding (preboard -> 90 days), and running consistent performance and feedback cycles. It includes step-by-step procedures, sample rubrics, checklists, and templates intended to keep candidate and new-hire experiences predictable, fair, and aligned with company values.

1) Hiring: process, roles, and scorecards

Intro: The hiring process balances speed, candidate experience, and quality-of-hire. People Ops partners with hiring managers to define role expectations, assess compensation fit, and coordinate interview panels. Managers are the hiring owner for their team and responsible for candidate evaluation and decisioning.

Quick role owner checklist:
- Write/approve the role profile and hiring criteria with People Ops.
- Define the core competencies and success metrics for first 6 months.
- Confirm interview panel and scheduling availability.
- Complete calibration with peer managers for level/ramp expectations.

Standard interview stages (recommended):
1. Recruiter screen (30 min) — culture, logistics, compensation expectations.
2. Hiring manager screen (30-45 min) — scope, high-level skills, role fit.
3. Technical assessment / homework (as required) — time-boxed, paid when >3 hours.
4. Panel interviews (3-4 interviews, 45-60 min each) — focused on core competencies (system design, coding, product sense, infra, security depending on role).
5. Final calibration and decision with hiring committee.

Interview rubric (example for IC engineering roles):
- Problem solving (1-5): clarity of thought, approach decomposition, tradeoffs.
- System design (1-5): scalability, reliability, cost-awareness, API surface.
- Implementation (1-5): correctness, testing, maintainability.
- Collaboration & communication (1-5): cross-team work, clear explanations.
- Role-specific skills (1-5): e.g., CUDA/kernel optimization, observability, or product ML.

Decision rules (recommended):
- Default passing threshold: average >= 3.5 and no score < 2 in a critical competency.
- If borderline, convene hiring committee (manager + 2 peers + recruiter + People Ops) for consensus.
- Document rationale in the candidate record before extending offer.

Offer and compensation
- Work with People Ops to prepare offers within the published leveling and comp bands.
- Include equity, base, bonus (if applicable), and expected start date.
- Offer approvals: manager -> director -> People Ops comp approver.

2) Preboarding and Day 0 preparations

Goal: remove friction so new hires can be productive in week 1.

Preboarding checklist (owner in parentheses):
- Confirm start date and first-week schedule with the new hire (Manager).
- Submit hardware and software requests to Eng Infra (Manager).
- Add to relevant Slack channels and calendar invites (Manager/People Ops).
- Assign a buddy and schedule intro meetings (Manager).
- Create initial onboarding plan with role-specific goals (Manager).
- Ensure access requests (G-Suite, GitHub, internal dashboards, Redwood Console demo accounts, infra tickets) are submitted 5 business days prior (Manager/IT).

Onboarding 30/60/90 plan (table):
| When | Owner | Deliverable / Outcomes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Day 0 | Manager & People Ops | Welcome pack, hardware, accounts, 1:1 schedule, buddy assigned |
| Week 1 | Manager & Buddy | Technical setup, team orientation, shadow meetings, first small ticket completion |
| 30 days | Manager | Clear 30-day goals, baseline OKRs for ramp, first feedback checkpoint |
| 60 days | Manager | Increased ownership of tasks, cross-team introductions, course-correct goals |
| 90 days | Manager | Performance checkpoint, promotion/ramp decisions, long-term goals set |

Suggested first-week schedule (high level):
- Day 1 AM: company orientation (People Ops), security & compliance briefing, and hardware setup.
- Day 1 PM: team welcome, team lunch (virtual/in-person), buddy pairing.
- Days 2-5: deep-dive sessions with key stakeholders, shadowing, small onboarding tasks.

Role-specific ramp examples
- Engineering (Serving Runtime): first 30 days — run the perf-suite locally, debug a low-risk regression; 60 days — own a small optimization; 90 days — lead an on-call rotation shift.
- Product/PM: first 30 days — complete roadmap readout and customer context; 60 days — own a minor feature spec; 90 days — drive cross-functional delivery.

3) Performance and feedback cycles

Principles:
- Frequent, specific feedback beats infrequent general feedback.
- Calibration and documentation reduce bias and aid promotion decisions.
- Managers own development conversations; People Ops supports process and appeals.

Cadence and artifacts:
- Continuous feedback: short notes in performance system or private doc after significant events.
- Formal check-ins: 1:1 weekly, 30/60/90 checkpoints for new hires.
- Quarterly performance review: self-assessment + manager assessment + calibration.
- Promotion cycle: documented achievements, peer feedback, manager recommendation, calibration panel.

Quarterly review process (step-by-step):
1. Manager notifies direct report of timeline and shares templates (Week 1 of quarter end).
2. Employee completes self-assessment (two weeks before review window).
3. Manager collects peer feedback (optional, targeted) and drafts manager assessment.
4. Calibration: managers and directors meet to normalize scores and outcomes.
5. Review conversation: manager shares outcomes, development plan, and comp changes (if any).
6. Finalize documentation and update HR records.

Feedback and difficult conversations
- Prepare: collect examples of behaviour/impact, reference role expectations and previous feedback.
- Deliver with care: describe behaviour, impact, and expected change; avoid surprises.
- Follow-up: set specific measurable goals, timeline, and check-ins (typically 30/60 day plan).
- Escalation: if no improvement, escalate to People Ops for formal performance improvement plan (PIP).

4) Manager responsibilities and best practices

Key manager responsibilities:
- Hiring and onboarding execution, candidate experience.
- Weekly 1:1s with direct reports that include career development time.
- Quarterly performance reviews and calibration prep.
- Running inclusive interviews and documenting evaluation.
- Ensuring psychological safety and equitable access to opportunities.

Manager best practices checklist:
- Maintain weekly 1:1 agenda shared in advance.
- Give at least one specific positive and one area to improve in every feedback conversation.
- Keep a running list of accomplishments and tickets for each report.
- Sponsor at least one high-potential IC for cross-team exposure per year.

5) Templates and examples

Candidate rejection email (short):
"Hi [Candidate],
Thank you for interviewing for [Role]. After careful consideration we will not be moving forward. We appreciate your time and wish you the best — please feel free to reach out if you’d like feedback.
Best, [Hiring Manager]"

30/60/90 manager checkpoint template (use in performance system):
- 30-day summary: onboarding progress, first deliverables, blockers.
- 60-day summary: autonomy, collaboration, next milestones.
- 90-day summary: ramp status, recommended ongoing objectives, learning needs.

Feedback example (format: Situation — Behaviour — Impact — Request):
- Situation: During sprint planning on 2026-01-12,
- Behaviour: you interrupted stakeholders frequently and didn’t allow clarifying questions,
- Impact: the team missed alignment and delivery uncertainty rose,
- Request: please pause after questions and invite clarifying discussion; I’ll coach on facilitation in next meeting.

6) Common policies and infra notes

Time off during probation: standard paid time off is available, but managers should coordinate re: critical ramp weeks.
Remote onboarding: ensure extra buddy check-ins and at least two in-person touchpoints within first 90 days if possible.
Security & compliance: all new hires must complete mandatory training in the first 14 days (security, data handling, incident reporting).

7) Promotion and leveling guidance (summary)

Promotions are evidence-based and manager-driven. For every promotion recommendation, submit:
- A clear case with examples mapped to the promotion rubric,
- Peer feedback and outcome metrics,
- Manager endorsement and suggested next-level responsibilities.

8) Escalations and People Ops handoffs

When to involve People Ops early:
- Complex compensation exceptions, visa/start-date issues, or counteroffers.
- Potential performance issues that may lead to PIP.
- Termination considerations or disciplinary matters.

Handoff checklist to People Ops:
1. Provide timeline and summary of actions taken.
2. Share documented feedback and improvement opportunities.
3. Confirm approvals and legal considerations.
